subject: Bridging credit & co-terming proposal for multi-year prepay - Acme Health
messages:
From: Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team is working through the legal redlines for the proposed 3-year annual prepay. I'm attaching our suggested redlines and an early-termination refund schedule — key asks:

- Full refund pro-rated in year 1 if we don't hit minimum consumption (with a 30-day notice)
- Capability to co-term this contract to our existing enterprise expiration on 2028-08-31
- No escrow requirement; prefer a capped credit/offset vs escrow

Can you and your legal review and propose where Redwood can be flexible on term economics? Attached: Acme_Proposed_Redlines.pdf

Thanks,

Brian O'Connell
Head of Procurement
Acme Health
Attachment: Acme_Proposed_Redlines.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

On Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0500 Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Evelyn,
>
> Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team is working through the legal redlines for the proposed 3-year annual prepay. I'm attaching our suggested redlines and an early-termination refund schedule — key asks:
>
> - Full refund pro-rated in year 1 if we don't hit minimum consumption (with a 30-day notice)
> - Capability to co-term this contract to our existing enterprise expiration on 2028-08-31
> - No escrow requirement; prefer a capped credit/offset vs escrow

Brian —

Appreciate the clarity. We're open to a bridging-credit approach instead of escrow; that preserves cashflow for you while protecting Redwood on early exit. High level proposal attached (bridging-credit-summary.xlsx):

- Year 1: 50% refundable (prorated by quarter), Year 2: 25% refundable, Year 3: no refund
- If co-terming to 2028-08-31, we'll amortize the credit over the remaining contractual months and apply an offset on renewal
- A 60-day notice clause for early termination; standard audit clauses to verify consumption

Marissa is copying pricing math (she'll follow with scenarios). If this is directionally acceptable, we'll draft contract language that maps to your redlines and pull legal in.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: bridging-credit-summary.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

Evelyn / Brian —

Adding the pricing view. Attached are three refund-impact scenarios with numbers aligned to usage ramp assumptions you shared:

Scenario A (customer-friendly): Year1 60% refund, Year2 40%, Year3 0% — results in higher short-term liability for Redwood
Scenario B (compromise): Year1 50%, Year2 25%, Year3 0% — lowers liability, retains incentive to stay
Scenario C (Redwood pref): Year1 30%, Year2 15%, Year3 0% — minimal refund exposure

Also modeled co-term offsets: if we co-term to 2028-08-31 we can give an upfront offset equal to the remaining months' amortized value vs a one-time bridging credit. See refund-scenarios.csv

Happy to walk through numbers on a call.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: refund-scenarios.csv (text/csv)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 08:55:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

Evelyn / Marissa —

Thanks for the scenarios. We prefer Scenario A from a procurement standpoint given our internal risk profile. Specific counter-proposal from legal:

- Year1: 100% refund pro-rated if minimum consumption not met (capped to six months of committed spend) with 30-day notice
- Year2: 60% refund, Year3: 20% refund
- Co-term to 2028-08-31 with a one-time co-term credit that does not reduce the refund calculation for Year1

We realize some asks are aggressive. If Redwood can move closer to Scenario A I'll route to our CFO for sign-off this week.

Sanjay Patel
VP, Vendor Management
Acme Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmehealth.com>, Brian O'Connell <brian.oconnell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 09:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

Sanjay —

Thanks for the transparency. To avoid a lengthy back-and-forth, Redwood can agree to a customer-forward compromise that balances your procurement needs and our financial controls. Final commercial offer (attached): final-offer-bridging.pdf

Key points:
- Year1: 50% refundable, but capped to six months of committed spend (prorated monthly)
- Year2: 25% refundable, Year3: 0%
- Co-term to 2028-08-31: Redwood will provide a one-time co-term credit equal to the amortized remaining months. That credit will be applied on renewal rather than reducing the initial refund calculation.
- Early termination requires 60 days' notice; standard audit rights retained

If that works, we've created a DocuSign envelope to speed execution: https://docusign.com/XYZ-DocuSign-Envelope-12345

I'll loop in legal if you accept; otherwise, happy to jump on a call tomorrow.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: final-offer-bridging.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Prepay redlines and refund schedule (Acme Health)

Evelyn —

Sending to finance and legal for exec approval once you confirm sending the final offer to the customer. I put the numbers into our prepay amortization template and this approach preserves ~65% of our ARR NPV vs scenario C.

Next steps:
- Confirm send (Evelyn)
- Finance to sanity-check P&L treatment (Karthik)
- If green, we route to legal for a quick redline and e-sign

—Marissa
